$comment: Declarative readiness evidence for the Manna progress report.
Why a hand-maintained file rather than inference: the statuses below are
CLAIMS, and a claim needs named evidence and a reviewer. Deriving them
automatically would mean guessing — and a dashboard that guesses
'VERIFIED' is worse than no dashboard, because it manufactures exactly
the false confidence the audit record exists to prevent.
So every entry carries an `evidence` string, and changing a status is a
reviewable diff in a pull request. Anything not actually checked is
NOT RUN or BLOCKED, never VERIFIED.
Permitted status values: VERIFIED, PARTIAL, BLOCKED, NOT RUN,
NOT APPLICABLE. No percentages — there is no defined denominator, so a

operational.name: Database backup and restore verification
operational.evidence: Decision 0005 Phase 0. A backup that has never been restored is not a backup. Procedure drafted at docs/runbooks/backup-restore-rehearsal.md; requires owner action

operational.name: Redis-backed rate limiting in production
operational.evidence: CONFIGURATION CONFIRMED, OPERATION NOT VERIFIED. The owner reports REDIS_URL is set for production (2026-10-20, name only; no value requested or held by this session). That is not the same claim as "limits are shared": lib/rate-limit.ts falls back to in-process counters on any Redis client or command failure, sets redisUnavailable=true, and deliberately does not log the error because it can embed the credential-bearing URL. The flag LATCHES — the only resets are test-only — so a degraded instance stays degraded until it recycles, with one generic stderr line as the sole signal. Operational proof needs POST /api/admin/operations/redis-rate-limit run against production with an admin session; that route performs an isolated set/get/delete and is already implemented and audited. Until that runs, treat shared limiting as configured but unproven.

operational.name: Branch protection enforcing required checks
operational.evidence: Re-verified 2026-10-19 after merging #63: GitHub reports master as protected:false, so NONE of the six passing checks is required. The protection-detail endpoint 403s for scope, but the branch record is authoritative on whether any protection exists. Passing != enforced.

operational.name: Schema migration versioning (decision 0005 Phase 2)
operational.evidence: schema_migrations plus registry, detection, drift and advisory-lock concurrency implemented and covered by 33 cases in lib/__tests__/migration-versioning.test.ts against fresh and populated PostgreSQL 16 databases. PARTIAL because baseline adoption has NOT been run against production and has no first-class entry point (measured: pnpm tsx and plain node both fail); and because whether the three migrations/ files were ever executed against production remains unknown by design.
